os-4-9.alt: Eight drawings of exocrine glands sunk into a surface epithelium. Glands at the top have one unbranched duct (simple); glands at the bottom have a branching duct system (compound). Glands on the right have tube-shaped secretory parts (tubular); glands on the left end in round sacs (alveolar, or acinar); one compound gland has both.

os-4-10.alt: Three rows of three gland cells on a basement membrane. Top row: vesicles from the Golgi apparatus fuse with the top of the cell and release their contents while the cell stays whole. Middle row: the top of the cell, packed with product, pinches off. Bottom row: a cell fills with product, breaks apart, and the whole cell becomes the secretion.
